source.title: Crash Risk and the Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with higher lagged down-to-up volatility (DUVOL), a crash-risk proxy, earn lower subsequent returns; a weekly long-low-crash-risk / short-high-crash-risk portfolio should earn positive net returns.
universe: Frozen ex-ante Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals listed by 2021-12-31, including later-delisted contracts where data exist. Each Monday retain top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
feature: For each asset and Monday, use the prior W completed daily close-to-close returns. Center by their window mean, split centered returns into down/up observations, compute log(sd_down/sd_up); signal is negative DUVOL so larger signal means lower crash risk.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long highest -DUVOL quintile / short lowest -DUVOL quintile, 0.5 gross each side.
execution: All feature/liquidity data end Sunday; rebalance Monday 00:00 UTC open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC of -DUVOL >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive high-minus-low signal spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 windows positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The source studies NCSKEW and DUVOL as crash-risk measures. This preregistration isolates DUVOL and uses rolling windows suitable for weekly trading with hourly-derived daily Binance perpetual data.
